```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="k02" data-src="../assets/learn/data/01-power-energy.json ../assets/learn/data/07-cost.json ../assets/learn/data/13-capstone.json ../assets/learn/data/town.json ../assets/learn/data/cf_targets.json ../assets/learn/data/k02-rates-efficiencies.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Rates and efficiencies, in five moves</p>
<ol>
<li>A rate is one amount per another: 10,791 kWh bought in a year ÷ 8,760 h = 1.232 kW, an average of 1,232 W bought from the grid.</li>
<li>Rates chain when the units cancel: 6.226 MMBtu per MWh × $3.85 per MMBtu = $23.97 per MWh, and × 52.91 kg CO₂ per MMBtu = 329 kg per MWh.</li>
<li>Efficiency = 3.412 MMBtu per MWh ÷ heat rate: 54.8% for the combined-cycle plant, 37.3% for the peaker (heat rate 9.142).</li>
<li>Efficiencies multiply going forward, and dividing undoes them: an 85% battery gives back 85 of 100 MWh; 100 MWh back needs 100 ÷ 0.85 = 117.6 MWh in, not 115.</li>
<li>A capacity factor is energy made ÷ the most possible over the same period; for a year, 150 MW × 8,760 h × 33.8% = 444,132 MWh.</li>
</ol>
<div class="k2-tables">
<!-- k2-rates:start (written by _tests/learn/test_k02-rates-efficiencies.js --write; do not edit) -->

<thead><tr><th scope="col">Rate</th><th scope="col">Unit</th><th scope="col">Worked on this page</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Average power bought from the grid</td><td>kW = kWh per hour</td><td>10,791 kWh ÷ 8,760 h = 1.232 kW</td></tr>
<tr><td>Heat rate</td><td>MMBtu per MWh</td><td>6.226 (combined-cycle), 9.142 (peaker)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fuel cost</td><td>$ per MWh</td><td>6.226 × $3.85 = $23.97</td></tr>
<tr><td>CO₂ at the plant</td><td>kg per MWh</td><td>6.226 × 52.91 = 329 kg</td></tr>
<tr><td>Efficiency</td><td>% (out ÷ in)</td><td>3.412 ÷ 6.226 = 54.8%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Round trip</td><td>% (back ÷ in)</td><td>117.6 MWh in, 100 MWh back at 85%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Capacity factor</td><td>% (made ÷ most possible)</td><td>150 MW × 8,760 h × 33.8% = 444,132 MWh</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<!-- k2-rates:end -->
</div>
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you work these out yourself, step by step.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-datanote"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><ul>
<li>A home's 10,791 <span class="lx-term" data-term="kilowatt-hour">kWh</span> a year: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=97&amp;t=3">EIA</a>, 2022 data, as in <a href="01-power-energy.html">lesson 1</a>.</li>
<li>Heat rates 6.226 and 9.142 <span class="lx-term" data-term="mmbtu">MMBtu</span> per MWh: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/aeo/assumptions/pdf/EMM_Assumptions.pdf">EIA, AEO2026 assumptions, Table 3</a> (April 2026). Gas $3.85 per MMBtu: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_07_04.html">EIA</a>, 2025 average. Both as in <a href="07-cost.html">lesson 7</a>.</li>
<li>52.91 kg CO₂ per MMBtu of gas: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/environment/emissions/co2_vol_mass.php">EIA</a> (checked 2 November 2026), as lessons 12 and 13 use it.</li>
<li>CO₂ boundary: gas burned at the plant only. Producing and delivering the gas, and building the plant, are outside it.</li>
<li>Lesson 0's town uses a rounded, illustrative 0.37 t (metric tonnes) of CO₂ per MWh instead.</li>
<li>3,412 Btu per kWh, so 3.412 MMBtu per MWh: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=107&amp;t=3">EIA FAQ on plant efficiency</a> (checked 3 November 2026).</li>
<li>85% round trip: <a href="13-capstone.html">lesson 13</a>'s battery, from <a href="https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy25osti/93281.pdf">NREL's 2025 battery cost study</a> (June 2025); <a href="09-storage.html">lesson 9</a>'s illustrative battery uses 80%.</li>
<li>Prairie Town's 150 MW wind farm is illustrative; 33.8% is U.S. wind in 2025: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/monthly/epm_table_grapher.php?t=epmt_6_07_b">EIA, Table 6.07.B</a> (released 23 October 2026).</li>
</ul></div>
```

## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="k2-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Rate</dt><dd>One amount per another, such as $ per MWh; its unit says what was divided by what.</dd>
<dt>Chaining rates</dt><dd>Multiply rates when a unit cancels: MMBtu per MWh × $ per MMBtu gives $ per MWh.</dd>
<dt>Heat rate and efficiency</dt><dd>Efficiency = 3.412 ÷ heat rate in MMBtu per MWh: a higher heat rate means a lower efficiency.</dd>
<dt>Losses in a chain</dt><dd>Stage efficiencies multiply: 54.8% × 85% = 46.6%. To go backwards, divide.</dd>
<dt>Capacity factor</dt><dd>Energy made ÷ the most possible in the same hours: a ratio with no unit.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>EIA's own units, and percent against percentage points</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Btu per kWh.** EIA quotes heat rates in Btu per kWh. 6,226 Btu per kWh is the same rate as 6.226 MMBtu per MWh: a million Btu per thousand kWh.
- **Efficiency in those units.** $\eta = 3{,}412 \div 6{,}226 = 54.8\%$, exactly as on this page.
- **Points.** From the peaker's 37.3% to the combined-cycle plant's 54.8% is 17.5 percentage points.
- **Percent.** Per MWh, the peaker burns $9.142 \div 6.226 = 1.47$ times the gas: 47% more. Say which one you mean.
- **Ratios hide a period.** A capacity factor needs its hours: [lesson 5](05-capacity-factor.html) uses 8,760 for a year.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Rates as fixed numbers in a model (a preview)</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Rates become fixed numbers.** A planning model multiplies each MWh a gas plant makes by rates like these: 6.226 × \$3.85 = \$23.97 of fuel and 0.329 t of CO₂. A real plant's heat rate changes with its output; a fixed one is a modeling choice.
- **Where next.** [Lesson 13](13-capstone.html) writes such a model in full, and [M3](m03-capacity-expansion.html) builds one in a notebook.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="k2-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="higher" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A plant with a higher heat rate is more efficient.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Heat rate is gas burned per MWh, so higher means more gas: 9.142 gives 37.3%, 6.226 gives 54.8%.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="add" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “To get 100 MWh out of an 85% battery, charge 115 MWh.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. 115 × 0.85 = 97.75 MWh. Divide instead: 100 ÷ 0.85 = 117.6 MWh.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="k2">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="fuel" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">The peaker burns 9.142 MMBtu of gas per MWh, and gas costs $3.85 per MMBtu. Its fuel cost per MWh?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">$2.37</li><li data-value="b">$35.20</li><li data-value="c">$12.99</li><li data-value="d">$0.42</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$35.20: 9.142 × 3.85, and MMBtu cancels. $2.37 divides instead; $12.99 adds numbers with different units.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="cf" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">A 100 MW plant made 438,000 MWh in a year of 8,760 hours. Its capacity factor?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">1,200%</li><li data-value="b">5%</li><li data-value="c">50%</li><li data-value="d">0.5%</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>50%: 438,000 ÷ (100 × 8,760) = 438,000 ÷ 876,000. Dividing by 365 days instead of 8,760 hours gives 1,200%, which no plant can reach.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="k2-drill"></div>
```
